content.introduction: According to Reuters, Asia-Pacific companies are expected to surpass their 2021 record for share and convertible bond fundraising driven by an AI boom. Indonesia is projected to have a larger trade surplus of about $630 million in August, while its inflation rate for September is expected to rise slightly. The Indian rupee has been one of the worst performers in Asia this quarter and over the last 30 days due to elevated crude prices and surging global bond yields. Singapore's state investor Temasek plans to open offices in Riyadh and Abu Dhabi in the first half of 2027 to seek investment and partnership opportunities across the Middle East. Meanwhile, Asian stocks dropped sharply with investors fearing the Middle East war could drive an oil shock that fuels inflation and delays interest rate cuts.
body:
Asia-Pacific companies are poised to challenge ​their 2021 record for share and convertible bond fundraising this year, as an AI boom ‌drives investment in chips, data centres and power systems.
 Indonesia was expected to record a larger trade surplus of about $630 ​million in August, while its inflation ‌rate for September was projected to rise slightly, according to a Reuters poll of economists. [...] The Indian rupee was among the worst performers in Asia this quarter and over the last 30 days, hit by worries over ​elevated crude prices and surging global bond yields that added to headwinds ‌for local assets.
 Singapore state investor Temasek said on Wednesday it planned to open offices in Riyadh ​and Abu Dhabi in the first half of 2027, ‌subject to approvals, seeking investment and partnership opportunities across the Middle East. [...] Indonesia's central bank has increased its purchases of government bonds in the secondary market ​in September in a bid to pump up liquidity, an ‌official said on Wednesday.
 Gold surrendered earlier gains and eased on Wednesday, ‌heading for a monthly decline, as higher energy prices eclipsed support from softer-than-expected U.S. inflation data that reduced expectations for an immediate Federal Reserve rate hike.

London's FTSE 100 ​rose on Wednesday as investors assessed stronger-than-expected GDP data, and was ‌on course for a monthly loss as persistent inflation concerns and rising bond yields dampened sentiment.
 The Indian rupee was among the worst performers in Asia this quarter and over the last 30 days, hit by worries over ​elevated crude prices and surging global bond yields that added to headwinds ‌for local assets. [...] US stock index futures were slightly higher on Wednesday as bond yields eased ​and some megacap and growth stocks ticked up heading into a crucial inflation report that could help shape ‌market expectations about the Federal Reserve's rate path.
 Scottish Mortgage Investment Trust said it had more than halved its China exposure ​over the past six years as it factored ‌in geopolitical and regulatory risks. [...] Indian student housing firm Elevate Campuses made a muted stock market debut on Wednesday, as investors ​weighed the company's growth prospects against elevated debt ‌and revenue concentration.

March 4 (Reuters) - Asian stocks dropped sharply on Wednesday, with investors dumping positions in chipmakers for fear the Middle East war will drive an oil shock that fuels inflation and delays interest rate cuts.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) fell 4.2%. Seoul's benchmark KOSPI (.KS11) shed more than 11% to trigger a circuit breaker, while Japan's Nikkei (.N225) and Taiwan's index (.TWII) dropped more than 4% each.

Sign up here. [...] "The impact on Asian markets has been higher because Asian economies are more vulnerable to the Strait of Hormuz closure and because in the run-up to the war, momentum trends were very sharp in many parts of Asia such as Korea.

"For markets to find a floor, we need signs of de-escalation on the war front or status quo which could then move the focus back to fundamentals."

RADHIKA RAO, SENIOR ECONOMIST, DBS BANK, SINGAPORE:
